He Got Game (1998)
He Got Game follows Jesus Shuttlesworth, one of the most highly recruited high school basketball players in the country, as he prepares to make one of the biggest decisions of his life. His talent has attracted attention from major colleges, coaches, and people looking to benefit from his future. At the same time, his father, Jake Shuttlesworth, is serving time in prison and is given an opportunity that could change both of their lives. 

In pop culture, He Got Game became one of the most influential basketball films of the late 1990s. Written and directed by Spike Lee and starring Ray Allen and Denzel Washington, the film brought together two major worlds, basketball and hip-hop culture. Ray Allen’s portrayal of Jesus was especially significant because he was an actual NBA player making his acting debut, giving the basketball scenes an authenticity that few sports movies could replicate.

On a broader cultural level, He Got Game examined the pressure placed on young athletes to succeed, particularly when their talent can become a business opportunity for coaches, schools, brands, families, and other people around them. It also explored fatherhood, forgiveness, sacrifice, and the difficult decisions that come with having a future everyone else wants to control.
